title: Why does reading in a car make you carsick? | So That's Why
description:
Little Q was reading a comic on the mountain road to Grandma's house. Halfway through, her head got dizzy and her tummy felt weird; but Dad, driving up front, was totally fine. Same car, same road, so why was she the only one feeling sick?

In this episode, the Chief and Little Q follow one car ride: first they use a cup of water as a comparison to see how the balance organs deep in your ear feel turns and braking, and what your eyes report; then they look at which report changes when you read, why blindfolded passengers still get sick, and the explanation most widely accepted in carsickness research, "sensory conflict": the reports don't match what the brain expects. Next they flip it around: some people get sick just sitting on a sofa watching racing on a screen. And finally they're honest about what this explanation still can't answer: why people differ so much, and why it's nausea, of all things.

This episode only covers what research has observed and today's explanations; it is not medical advice. The illustrations were made with AI; they are diagrams, not anatomy charts. The source of every claim is listed in the references below.
